en.title: Minimum Operations for Parallel Task Execution (MathWorks #21)
en.description: In each round, choose one task as the main task and run it for x seconds, while every other task runs for y seconds; once a task's accumulated run time reaches its required time, it finishes and leaves. Find the minimum number of rounds needed to finish all tasks. The original MathWorks #21 statement is truncated midway in the OAMaster page snapshot; the original Markdown of the same version in the fixed source repository states y < x in full, and its rules, function signature, and constraints are the same as those of Snowflake #15. The public examples and standard input format below were compiled by CSWork and are not source examples.
en.input: The first line contains n x y, and the second line contains n positive integers executionTime. 1≤n≤100000, 1≤executionTime[i]≤10^9, 1≤y<x≤10^9.
en.output: Output the minimum number of operations needed to finish all tasks.
en.explanation: Binary search on the number of operations T. With T rounds, every task gets at least T·y of base execution; each main-task operation provides x−y extra toward the remaining demand, so task i still needs to be chosen as the main task ceil(max(0, executionTime[i]−T·y)/(x−y)) times. T is feasible when the total of these counts does not exceed T.
hints: For a candidate number of rounds T, compute how many extra main-task executions each task still needs; if the total is ≤T, everything can finish.
